title: GM Unveils Autonomous Silverado 3500HD for the Army
key_facts: GM Defense showed a fully autonomous, electric pickup-based unmanned ground vehicle concept at the Association of the United States Army meeting on Monday.
It is built on the Silverado 3500HD platform with a 100 kWh energy-storage system and a maximum payload of 8,000 pounds.
GM Defense says it is meant for 'silent logistics and casualty evacuation'.
The self-driving software comes from Scout AI's Gx Ground Agent.
The defence configuration adds a Locust X3 laser for countering drones and an acoustic drone sensor.
GM Defense president Steve duMont is quoted on the launch.
quote_evidence: GM Defense showed a fully autonomous, electric-drive pickup at the Association of the United States Army Annual Meeting and Exposition on Monday.
Its Unmanned Ground Vehicle concept trades internal combustion for silent electric drive, with functional trials targeted for 2027.
The autonomous driving stack comes from Scout AI's Gx Ground Agent, and the vehicle relies on drive-by-wire controls.
why_it_matters_hint: A concept shows carmakers moving into driverless military logistics vehicles.
notes: Concept only; trials not before 2027. Day of week from article; date derived.
